title: Pilot Sync - Benchmark Sprint 1 (Ivybridge vs Incumbent)
topics: Next steps and pilot success criteria
summary: Weekly pilot sync reviewing Sprint 1 benchmark artifacts. Redwood and Ivybridge reviewed throughput and latency deltas versus incumbent provider. Main items: Redwood shows 15-28% unit-cost improvement with similar median latency but occasional 99p spikes; tuning plan covers batching, prefix caching, and routing thresholds. Action items agreed for deeper load tests, raw log handoff, and pricing delta for dedicated slots.
action_items: Alex Morgan: Share detailed bench spreadsheet and raw tail latency logs by 2025-01-30 (https://redwood.app/bench/ivybridge-sprint1)
Jordan Lee: Run 50k token loadtest with 4k context and include KV warm/cold scenarios; due 2025-02-03
Maya Chen: Push routing/playbook config and canary policy to Ivybridge repo and demo on next call; due 2025-02-05
Priya Rao: Provide compliance list (SOC2 scope and any additional regs) for pilot by 2025-02-02
next_steps: Schedule side-by-side live demo with dedicated slot (Alex to propose times)
Provide pricing delta and committed slot options for Dedicated vs Hosted (Alex)
Initiate SSO test account and KMS handshake for Private eval (Priya + Maya)
Plan 2-hour throughput run against incumbent baseline with identical prompts and seed (Jordan)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-01-28
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Sam (Ivybridge CTO), Priya (Ivybridge SRE), Jordan (Ivybridge ML eng)
Shared artifacts: Bench sheet: https://redwood.app/bench/ivybridge-sprint1 , Deck: https://redwood.app/decks/pilot-ivybridge.pdf

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick check, agenda is a short walkthrough of the Sprint 1 numbers, talk tuning, and agree next steps. Maya will lead the bench bits.
00:24 Maya: Hi team. I pulled the main charts into the sheet — median token latency, p95, p99, and throughput across 1k/5k/20k concurrent sessions. Note: some of the p99 numbers include a cold-KV window so they look a bit worse.
00:46 Sam: Right, saw that note. Can you restate the headline versus our incumbent? We care about tail latency — our users hit the p99 and it matters.
01:05 Maya: Sure. For the 1k concurrent synthetic run, median latency was ~120ms vs incumbent 115ms, so parity. Throughput was about 18% higher on Redwood which maps to about 22% lower per-token cost in that profile. p99 though — we saw 420ms spikes during KV cold starts; incumbent was around 290ms in our test.
01:34 Priya: Are those KV spikes on routing or are they model quantization effects? We noticed spikes when a request landed on a node that hadn't seen the prefix.
01:49 Maya: Great question. It's mostly KV cache warmup — our continuous batching interacts with the cache eviction heuristics. There's also a small quant-dequant overhead on the 8-bit path but it's minor vs KV.
02:10 Jordan: I ran a separate run with forced warm caches and p99 dropped to ~310ms so that confirms it. We should look at pre-warming or prefix caching.
02:30 Alex: Important to call out cost tradeoffs. If we pre-warm aggressively you'll raise steady-state unit cost. The recommendation we gave in deck is a hybrid: pre-warm top 200 prefixes and rely on on-demand for the rest.
02:54 Sam: Ok that seems reasonable. For regulatory reasons we also want to know how Dedicated would change this. If we move to a dedicated pool, does the KV behavior change?
03:12 Maya: Dedicated reduces cross-tenant eviction frequency; so warm rates increase and p99 improves. In our internal sims dedicated reduced p99 spikes by ~18% in similar workloads, so you might hit incumbent parity on tails. We'll include those numbers in the pricing delta.
03:31 Priya: Network wise, will there be region routing? We saw higher latency for traffic hitting the eu-west nodes from us-east.
03:46 Maya: We ran region-local experiments — routing policy can pin to region to avoid cross-region hops. There's a short-term tradeoff of capacity constraints; if region capacity saturates we can fallback to nearest region with a policy you set.
04:05 Jordan: On quantization — we tested 8-bit and a mixed 4-bit variant. 4-bit saved ~30% compute but introduced some jitter in the first 50 tokens of long-context prompts; not huge but noticeable in hallucination-sensitive flows.
04:26 Sam: For our use-case hallucination is risky. We prefer stable behavior over micro-cost savings. Likely we want 8-bit baseline.
04:37 Maya: That aligns with our suggestion — 8-bit quant + targeted 4-bit for non-critical routes.
04:46 Alex: Can we pivot to the throughput graphs — Maya?
04:51 Maya: Yes. For throughput we ran ramp tests to saturation. Redwood sustained 5% higher sustained QPS at equal latency, and peak throughput was 11% higher before latency degraded. Incumbent however had slightly lower variance in the 5-15 minute sustained window — their autoscaler is tuned differently.
05:17 Priya: Do you have the autoscale/slot config you used? We need to reproduce.
05:23 Maya: Sheet includes the cluster config: batch size ranges, concurrency per worker, and kernel selection flags. See tab "run-configs". Will attach raw logs as well.
05:34 Sam: One odd thing — on one run the incumbent beat you on p50 by ~10ms. Any idea?
05:41 Maya: That was likely their more aggressive prefetching and slightly different kernel opt path for short sequences. We think with minor kernel flag adjustments we can close that 10ms gap. It's not systematic.
05:57 Jordan: We also noticed a difference in prompt tokenization — their tokenizer strips some whitespace so effective token count was lower which helps median latency. Not Redwood's fault but worth aligning prompt preproc.
06:18 Alex: Good catch. We'll help normalise tokenization in both runs.
06:24 Maya: Next, routing/fallback tests. We ran a simulated outage and flipped to fallback model variant (smaller model) and saw correctness drift but latency remained within SLA. This is the graceful degradation playbook.
06:40 Priya: For compliance we need audit logs of every fallback. Is that recorded?
06:47 Maya: Yes — we log route decisions with timestamps and token counts; the audit export will be included.
06:55 Sam: On the unit-cost side can you show savings at 10M tokens/day?
07:03 Maya: At 10M tokens/day, using the current profile (mix of chat/completions), Redwood delta is roughly 18-22% lower TCO in the hosted scenario. Dedicated committed slots push savings to ~30% vs the incumbent because of lower amortized overhead and better batch packing. Exact numbers in the price appendix.
07:26 Alex: We'll send a scenario spreadsheet with committed tiers.
07:30 Jordan: For the long-context tests (4k) there was a big drop in throughput. Any mitigation?
07:36 Maya: Yes, KV streaming and shard-aware routing help. Also smaller model variants for short-turns can improve mixed workloads.
07:46 Sam: We have a mixed workload in prod — 70% short, 30% long context. Any recommended default?
07:55 Maya: Start with a mixed routing policy: default to full model for long contexts, route <=256 tokens to an optimized short-turn model. That gives ~20% throughput uplift for the short-turn portion.
08:10 Priya: We need to validate that short-turn model doesn't drop quality for any keys — Jordan will run evals.
08:16 Jordan: Yep will run eval set A/B and report.
08:19 Alex: Let's fast-forward to agreed tuning plan — Maya?
08:23 Maya: Actionable tuning: 1) Lock kernel flags to the set that gave best median; 2) Implement prefix caching for top prefixes; 3) Configure routing policy for mixed workload; 4) Run 2-hour side-by-side with identical seeds and tokenization; 5) Try dedicated slot sim to show tail improvements.
08:46 Sam: Sounds good. On the side-by-side test, how do we make sure it's apples-to-apples? Tokenization, prompt normalization, same input rate, same random seeds?
08:56 Maya: All that and we will use the same client harness; I'll publish the harness repo link. Also we'll include a small harness script to freeze warm caches for the cold-start case.
09:13 Priya: Security note — before we run the dedicated sim we need a data handling doc and KMS flow. I can't sign off without that.
09:21 Alex: Understood — I'll share our KMS sequence and the Private deployment checklist.
09:27 Maya: There's also a small observation: at the highest concurrency the Greenwood (typo: meant Redwood) batching window occasionally coalesces very large batches and you get a latency tail. We're tuning batch window size to cap that.
09:44 Jordan: Did you mean Greenwood? (laugh)
09:46 Maya: Sorry, yes typo, Redwood.
09:49 Sam: (laugh) okay.
09:52 Alex: Any blockers on our side?
09:56 Priya: Need the SOC2 scoping and IP flow doc. Also a short SLA draft for Dedicated.
10:03 Alex: We have a standard SLA PDF — will attach.
10:07 Maya: I'll also include kernel flags and the exact bench configs.
10:12 Sam: For the next call I'd like to see the side-by-side plan scheduled and the expected improvement numbers for p99 when using Dedicated.
10:20 Alex: Noted. We'll shoot for 48 hours turnaround on the bench sheet and pricing delta.
10:24 Jordan: Quick question — will Redwood's realtime streaming behave differently under quantized models? We saw a few dropped tokens in the 4-bit runs.
10:32 Maya: Streaming is slightly more sensitive, yes — 8-bit is recommended for streaming-heavy flows. We'll annotate the sheet per-route.
10:39 Priya: Can we get a low-level runbook on how to toggle fallback policies? Ops wants steps.
10:45 Maya: Will produce a runbook and short video.
10:49 Alex: Ok let's summarize next steps.
10:52 Alex: Action items recap: Alex share bench + SLA + pricing delta by 2025-01-30. Maya push run-configs and routing playbook by 2025-02-05. Jordan run 50k token warm/cold tests and long-context eval by 2025-02-03. Priya share SOC2 scoping and KMS handshake details by 2025-02-02.
11:18 Sam: Good recap. We'll aim to have SRE and security review those docs.
11:25 Alex: Any other questions?
11:28 Priya: No, thanks. We'll align internally and queue the side-by-side.
11:33 Alex: Great, thanks everyone. Wrap up.

End of transcript.
notes: Call ended with clear action items and agreement to run side-by-side dedicated sim. Minor transcription typos present (Greenwood).
